definition: The word for a technique or tradition and a year when at least one of its rules names the topic favourably and none names it unfavourably or as mixed. Modifier rules do not count.
The word for a technique or tradition and a year when at least one of its rules names the topic unfavourably and none names it favourably or as mixed. Modifier rules do not count.
The word for a technique or tradition and a year when its rules name the topic both favourably and unfavourably, or when one rule itself states a mixed result.
The word for a technique or tradition and a year when none of its rules names a direction for the topic. It is silence and is not a good or a bad year.
A technique with nothing said in a year. It may carry a stated reason, such as that it needs the sex convention.
A statement that marks the topic as active or says where a count reaches, without a direction. Pointers are counted apart and never change the word.
The display word for a pointer.
The one-line summary of a year that lists the techniques under the four words.
The technique a practitioner would name, such as the luck pillar or the mahadasha, which the forecast shows in place of a clock.
A rule about the chart alone, without dates. These statements are listed first and take no part in a year's word.
A rule about the planet, pillar or sign that rules a stretch of time.
A rule about an event inside a period, such as a transit or an arriving pillar.
A rule that qualifies other rules, such as a table or an obstruction.
The display of years in which techniques counted on different time scales gave the same word for the same topic. It does not say that the outcome follows.
A set of techniques counted from one clock, which count as one voice in the agreement display.
The badge on a dated statement. It says that no rule about the natal chart gates the statement; the engine has no gate semantics in this release.
The badge for I Ching statements, whose grades are a construction of the project on the old texts.
The badge on every statement for the topic relationships, because the result there can change with a named setting, such as the sex convention.
The badge for health statements, which state tendencies and say nothing about diagnosis.
The badge for a rule whose source was not opened by the project.
The badge for a statement whose recorded emphasis was set to 1 by a setting. The emphasis is the project's own and no source gives it.
The badge for a statement computed under a choice that departs from the source, for example whole-sign houses where Lilly used Regiomontanus cusps.
The sex the chart is read as, which fixes the direction of the BaZi luck pillars and which rules apply. The engine never guesses it.
A record of events a person enters, to be compared with forecasts frozen beforehand. It is the project's own addition and is not yet scored.
A forecast stored with a hash before the events are entered, so that only events entered after the freeze can be compared with it.
Comparing a forecast with events that were known before it was made.
The share of statements that matched events, as a scorecard would count them. The forecast does not give one.
A view of at most 62 days that shows the character of a period, used for the I Ching and for Lilly's day statements.
Divination based on time attributes. A report defines it as all divination techniques that take temporal parameters as their primary variables.
source: Lackner 2011, p. 4; Hanson in fate no. 10, p. 21

definition: An adjective, from a Greek word, used in scholarship for the divinatory arts. A newsletter report says it is anachronistic for some early Chinese methods, that "divination" is not ideal either, and that there is no perfect word.
A technique that reads signs, times or figures for what is to come.
Used in this project for stating what is to come, by any method.

The study of the relation between calendar time and daily fortune. The editors of the day-book volume define it as ideas, practices and texts in all cultures that relate time as expressed in the calendar to daily fortune.

A calendar with a miscellany. Lackner describes a modern all-purpose almanac as a calendar core with yin-yang, the Eight Trigrams, calculation of fate from the Eight Cyclical Signs, feng shui and recipes around it.
An umbrella term for schemes, tables, plans, topographical maps and figures.
The explanation that normally accompanies a cosmological diagram.
Fate or destiny. For Wang Chong it is conferred by Heaven at birth, and it is a general tendency named by the categories ji and xiong.
The auspicious and the inauspicious, the divinatory categories into which Wang Chong puts destiny. In the Changes they register success or failure.
Words of the Changes that register small faults (hui and lin) and the repair of transgressions (wujiu).
Knowing fate and establishing fate. Smith glosses the *Changes* as letting humans know fate and also do something about it.
The art that Lackner renders as calculation of fate from the Eight Characters and classes as chronomancy.
A name that a newsletter report gives for bazi suanming.
Verification, the coming true of a prognostication, which a fellow's project treats as the other side of prognostication.
source: IKGF project page of Zhou Zhenhe

definition: Anecdotes that a compiler of a Qing morality book offered as proof that a practice had worked.
The chart of eight characters, the stem and branch of the year, month, day and hour of a moment, which the engine computes. The project uses the name BaZi for the chart.
A stem and a branch together, for the year, the month, the day or the hour.
One of ten signs (Jia 甲, Yi 乙, Bing 丙, Ding 丁, Wu 戊, Ji 己, Geng 庚, Xin 辛, Ren 壬, Gui 癸), each with an element and a polarity.
One of twelve signs (Zi 子, Chou 丑, Yin 寅, Mao 卯, Chen 辰, Si 巳, Wu 午, Wei 未, Shen 申, You 酉, Xu 戌, Hai 亥), each with an element and an animal.
The sixty pairs that stems and branches make in order; the engine counts days, months and years by it.
Wood, fire, earth, metal and water, which each stem and branch carries.
The two polarities of the stems and branches. They decide which of two ten gods a stem is and the direction of the luck pillars.
The stem of the day pillar. Every other stem in the chart is judged by its relation to it.
A class the engine derives by comparing the support the day master gets from the chart with what drains it. The limits between the classes are the project's own.
Names for the relation of any other stem to the day master by element and polarity: 比肩, 劫財, 食神, 傷官, 偏財, 正財, 七殺, 正官, 偏印, 正印. The English names are trade usage.
The ten gods 正財 (direct wealth) and 偏財 (indirect wealth): the element that the day master overcomes, 偏財 for the same polarity and 正財 for the other.

original: 官殺, 正官, 七殺
definition: The element that overcomes the day master: 七殺 for the same polarity and 正官 for the other.
The element that generates the day master: 偏印 for the same polarity and 正印 for the other.
The element the day master generates: 食神 for the same polarity and 傷官 for the other.
The same element as the day master: 比肩 for the same polarity and 劫財 for the other.
The stems held inside an earthly branch. The engine uses them to find roots and ten gods.
The principal hidden stem of a branch, which the engine weighs above the middle and residual ones.
A hidden stem in a branch that equals or generates the element of the day stem.

The state of the day master in the month, by how the element of the month branch stands to the element of the day stem: the same (wang), generating it (xiang), generated by it (xiu), overcome by it (qiu), or overcoming it (si). The first two are in season (得令).
The twelve stages of a stem round the twelve branches, counted forward for yang stems and backward for yin stems.
The elements that the balance method names as helpful or harmful for this chart.
The method that names favourable elements from whether the day master is strong or weak.
The element that connects two opposed strong forces. The project offers it as a variant.

A ten-year pillar counted from the month pillar, forward or backward by the sex the chart is read as and the polarity of the year stem. The first opens at an age found by scaling the interval to the next jie (forward) or the previous jie (backward) at three days to the year.
The stem and branch of a year, which turns at Lichun by default.
Beginning of Spring, the solar term at which the engine turns the BaZi year by default.
One of twenty-four points of the Sun's course. The twelve jie open the BaZi months and the twelve zhongqi fall between them.
The double-hour from 23:00 to 01:00. Under the project's default convention zi23 the day pillar advances when it begins.
The two branches left unused by the day pillar's ten-day group. A branch in the chart equal to one of them is flagged as void, which is not read as bad by itself.
What a natal pillar stands for: the year pillar the ancestors, the month pillar the parents, the day branch the spouse, the hour pillar the children.

term: cover the head, cut the feet
definition: A luck pillar whose stem overcomes the element of its branch, or whose branch overcomes or fails to generate the element of its stem. The force of the wanted element on the capped or cut half of the pillar is halved.
A luck or year pillar identical to the day pillar (repeat), or whose branch is the six-clash of the day branch and whose stem stands four or six places from the day stem (reversal).

term: year and luck pillar the same
definition: The year pillar equals the luck pillar in stem and branch.
A luck pillar and a year pillar whose stems overcome one another and whose branches clash.
The pairs Zi and Wu, Chou and Wei, Yin and Shen, Mao and You, Chen and Xu, Si and Hai.
The pairs Zi and Chou, Yin and Hai, Mao and Xu, Chen and You, Si and Shen, Wu and Wei.
A group of three branches: Shen, Zi, Chen for water; Hai, Mao, Wei for wood; Yin, Wu, Xu for fire; Si, You, Chou for metal.
The two branches that the tables give for the day stem. When a luck or year branch equals one of them, the rule flags a noble helper period.
A branch given by the three-harmony group of the year or day branch. When a luck or year branch equals it, the rule flags a moving period: travel, relocation or a change of post.
A branch given by the three-harmony group, the second of the twelve stages. When a luck or year branch equals it, the rule marks relationships as active.
The branch that follows the lu branch of a yang day stem. The rule reads a period of the blade as a time of excess or conflict.
The lu branch of a day stem. When a luck or year branch equals it, the rule reads a period of income and standing.
A name and element given to each of the sixty pairs. The engine's thirty English names are the project's popular glosses.
The twelve day officers (jianchu), the twenty-eight lodges (xiu) of the almanac day cycle, and the nine-star year count (zibai), all counted by the engine.
The year branch of the twelve-year count, which the project's registry of correspondences relates to the circuit of Jupiter.
In a lecture abstract, the dangerous year ghost of the Chinese calendar, among the "superstitions" that the Jesuit Magalhaes attacked.
The project's name for the rules of the *Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra*, the *Phaladeepika* and Raman, read in English translation.
A zodiac measured from a fixed zero point among the stars and not from the equinox. The engine uses the Lahiri zero point.
The offset between tropical and sidereal longitude. The engine uses the true value, anchored on 21 March 1956.
The rising sign at the moment. Houses are counted from it by whole signs.
One of twelve places counted by whole sign from the Lagna. A rule that names a house uses the engine's table of what each house concerns.
The planet that owns the sign of the house.
One of the equal divisions of the sidereal zodiac into lunar mansions, each with a lord.
The system of planetary periods that totals 120 years. The engine takes years as 365.25 days.
The major period of the vimshottari system, ruled by one planet.
The sub-period within a mahadasha, ruled by one planet.
The angular houses from the Lagna. The engine's list is 1, 4, 7 and 10.
The trine houses from the Lagna. The engine's list is 1, 5 and 9.
A named combination of planets.
A yoga of a kendra lord and a trikona lord that exchange signs, stand together in a kendra or trikona, stand in each other's kind of house or fully aspect each other.
A single planet that owns both a kendra and a trikona.
A planet read as helpful or harmful for a given Lagna by the houses it owns.
A planet that owns the 2nd or 7th house. The rule flags strain on health and says it is not a prediction.
The state of a planet by sign: exalted, in its moolatrikona, in its own sign, in a friend's, neutral, in an enemy's or debilitated. Debilitation is the seventh sign from exaltation.
In the same sign. The engine uses no orb for this.

term: Saturn from the Moon, Jupiter from the Moon
definition: The sign Saturn or Jupiter is passing, counted from the sign of the natal Moon.
An obstruction: a planet's good transit is cancelled when another planet stands at the same time in the paired house.
The project's name for the rules of Lilly's *Christian Astrology* (1647), with Valens and Bonatti.
The birth chart; a thing is radical when it belongs to the birth chart.
The degree of the ecliptic rising on the eastern horizon, the degree culminating, and the degree opposite the Midheaven.
Houses counted as whole signs from the Ascendant sign. Lilly used Regiomontanus cusps, which the engine does not compute, so statements that name a house say so.
Whether the Sun is above the horizon (day chart) or below it (night chart). The engine uses it for triplicity and for the order of firdaria.
The sign a planet owns. The domicile lord of a sign is the planet that owns it.
The sign where a planet is strongest, and the opposite sign where it is weakest.
The sign opposite a planet's domicile.
A group of three signs of one element, each with lords. The engine uses Dorotheus's lords.
The unequal divisions of a sign that each belong to a planet. The engine uses the Egyptian bounds.
A division of ten degrees of a sign that belongs to a planet, in Chaldean order.
A planet that holds no essential dignity in the sign it stands in. A planet in its own face or term is not peregrine.
The standing a planet has from the sign and degree it stands in.
The standing a planet has from its house, its aspects and its relation to the Sun.
Houses 1, 4, 7 and 10; houses 2, 5, 8 and 11; houses 3, 6, 9 and 12.
A relation of two points by distance along the ecliptic: conjunction, sextile, square, trine, opposition. The orb is the allowed distance from the exact angle, as Lilly gives it.
A planet so near the Sun that the source reads it as weakened. The limit is in the engine's table.
Jupiter and Venus; Saturn and Mars.
The planet, house or point that stands for the matter asked about. The significators of wealth are those the rule names.

term: Part of Fortune, Lot of Fortune
definition: A point found from the Ascendant, Sun and Moon: Ascendant plus Moon minus Sun by day, Ascendant plus Sun minus Moon by night.
A point of the chart moved one sign for each year from birth; the sign it reaches names the year's sign and lord.
The domicile lord of the sign the profected Ascendant has reached.
The medieval scheme of nine planetary periods that total seventy-five years, each divided into sub-periods in Chaldean order.
The chart cast for the moment each year when the Sun returns to its birth longitude. Lilly calls it the revolution.
A planet passing over a point of the birth chart.
Valens's count from a starting point by the year's number. The planets standing in the sign the count reaches receive the year; if the sign is empty, its domicile lord does.
A year that Valens marks as troublesome, when the year's sign is the sign of the new or full Moon before birth, or its square or opposite.
The Classic of Changes. The project reads the *Zhouyi* text and the *Xici zhuan*, and the Han calendar parts that are attested elsewhere.
A figure of six lines, each broken or unbroken. There are sixty-four.
A figure of three lines. There are eight.

original: 卦辭 guaci, 爻辭 yaoci
definition: The text attached to a hexagram, and the text attached to one of its lines.
The Han calendar that gives hexagrams to stretches of the year, in the scheme of six days and seven parts, beginning with Zhong Fu at the winter solstice.
One of twelve hexagrams, one for each month, growing (xi) or waning (xiao).
Kan, Zhen, Li and Dui, which take a short allotment at each solstice and equinox in the scheme the project offers as Jing Fang's.
The Tang calendar in which Yi Xing adopted Meng Xi's gua qi scheme.
A text that the project cites only for beginning the gua qi count at Zhong Fu.

term: Fu Xi circle, xiantian, Former Heaven
definition: The arrangement of the sixty-four hexagrams, also called the Former Heaven sequence, that Smith describes as Shao Yong's: a square of the sixty-four enclosed by a circle in another order.
The arrangement of the sixty-four hexagrams on the tropical zodiac that twentieth-century systems use.
The gua qi hexagram that rules an instant. The forecast shows it by period only.
The part of a statement that names a journey, an audience, a marriage, an illness or goods, which the engine grades on its own.
A mechanical mark given to a statement by its verdict words. It is a construction of the project and is marked experimental.
